data.name: Injila
data.long_meaning: Injilah means 'news' or 'message' in Arabic. It is derived from the Arabic root 'n-j-l', which translates to 'to send, to deliver, or to announce'. Injila is a significant term in Islamic tradition, referring to the Gospel or the scripture sent to the People of the Book (Christians and Jews) by God.

It is often associated with the teachings of the Bible, specifically those related to Prophet Isa (Jesus) and his mission on Earth. In Islamic tradition, Injilah represents a crucial dialogue between the three Abrahamic faiths: Islam, Christianity, and Judaism.

The Quran asserts that God sent the Injil (Gospel) to Jesus and his followers to guide them towards the righteous path. This holy scripture serves as a testament to God's loving guidance and compassion for humanity. The study and interpretation of the Injil (as mentioned in the Quran) is essential for Muslims seeking to deepen their understanding of God's message to all of humanity.
